title: HookSchema.condition's @example is SQL where the slot is CEL — it does not compile, and it contradicts the .describe() on the next line
body:
Out-of-scope finding from #6763 / the spec TSDoc `@example` gate. Recorded per Prime Directive #10, unassigned.

Filed rather than fixed because `packages/spec/src/**` belongs to the `domain:spec` / `domain:spec-surface` seats, and #6763 landed in `domain:spec-tooling`. The gate PR exempts this site with a reason naming it as a real defect pending transfer, so the gate arrives green; deleting that exemption is part of this card's fix.

## The defect

`packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts:236`:

```
   * @example "status = 'active' AND amount > 1000"
   */
  condition: ExpressionInputSchema.optional().describe('Predicate (CEL); hook runs only when TRUE. e.g. P`record.status == "closed" && record.amount > 1000`'),
```

The `@example` and the `.describe()` are one line apart and disagree about the dialect. The slot is `ExpressionInputSchema` — canonical CEL, ADR-0058 D1 — and the `.describe()` spells the canonical form correctly. The `@example` is SQL on three counts: `=` for `==`, `AND` for `&&`, and bare `status` / `amount` where a record-scoped expression binds the record as the `record` namespace.

## Measured

The verdict is the platform's own `validateExpression` from `@objectstack/formula` — the same call `os build` / `os validate` makes:

| source | `validateExpression('value', src, { scope: 'record' })` |
|:--|:--|
| **`status = 'active' AND amount > 1000`** (as shipped) | **`invalid CEL value: Unexpected character: =`** |
| `record.status == 'active' && record.amount > 1000` | clean |
| `record.status == "active" && record.amount > 1000` | clean |

Note that the operators fail *first*: even after `=` becomes `==` and `AND` becomes `&&`, the bare `status` and `amount` would still resolve to nothing and the predicate would silently evaluate to null — the #5116 shape. So it is wrong twice over, and the second half is the silent one.

## Impact

Same class as #6641, one slot over: a schema's own `@example` is the first-hand transcription source an author (often an AI author, ADR-0033) copies. Copy this one and the hook's `condition` does not compile. This is the declared-not-enforced shape of Prime Directive #10 — the schema advertises an authoring form the runtime refuses.

It is a second live instance of the class #6763 recorded, found by measurement rather than by hand, which is what the earlier findings-round grading named as this class's promotion condition.

## Suggested fix

One line, matching the dialect the slot's own `.describe()` already teaches:

```diff
-   * @example "status = 'active' AND amount > 1000"
+   * @example "record.status == 'active' && record.amount > 1000"
```

Then delete the `HookSchema.condition` entry from `EXEMPT_EXAMPLES` in `packages/lint/scripts/check-doc-formula-expressions.mjs`. The gate is self-invalidating in that direction: leaving an exemption over a now-clean example is itself an error, so the cleanup cannot be forgotten silently.

Worth confirming while there: whether `active` is the status value the example means, since the `.describe()`'s own illustration uses `closed`.

## Related

#6763 (the gate that found it), #6641 / PR #6729 (the first instance of the class), ADR-0058 D1 (CEL is canonical), #5116 (the bare-reference half).
